title: 로마자 표기 읽기: Seoul, Busan, Gyeongbokgung
objective: By the end, you can read romanized place names such as Seoul, Busan and Gyeongbokgung and write them in Hangul.
summary: Match Korean romanization on signs and maps to Hangul.

task.title: Read and write romanization
task.line: Use the four rules on page 1 to change romanization into Hangul, or Hangul into romanization.

words.meaning: Busan (a port city in the south)
words.exampleMeaning: I'm going to Busan this weekend.
I'm meeting a friend in Myeongdong.

letters.letter: ㅓ = eo · ㅕ = yeo · ㅡ = eu
letters.sound: Two letters, one vowel: 서 [서] is seo, not 'se-o'.
letters.as: eo like 'u' in 'up'; eu like 'oo' with spread lips.

letters.letter: ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ = g d b / k t p
letters.sound: g, d, b before a vowel; k, t, p at the end: 복 = bok.
letters.as: Tense sounds are not marked: 경복궁 [경복꿍] = Gyeongbokgung.

letters.sound: r before a vowel, l at the end: 서울 = Seoul.
letters.as: r is a light tap, like 'tt' in American 'butter'.

letters.sound: Silent at the start; ng at the end: 강 = gang.
letters.as: Like 'ng' in 'sing', with no hard g at the end.

exercises: Choose the Hangul for each place name: ① Daegu (대구 / 대고) ② Jeonju (전주 / 정주) ③ Suwon (수원 / 서원)
Write each place name in romanization: ① 남산 ② 강남 ③ 동대문
Fill in the blank with g, k, b or p: ① 고기 → _ogi ② 대학 → daeha_ ③ 밥 → ba_
Write each word in Hangul: ① Gyeongju ② geurim ③ Hangeul
answers: ① 대구 ② 전주 ③ 수원
① Namsan ② Gangnam ③ Dongdaemun
① g (gogi) ② k (daehak) ③ p (bap)
① 경주 ② 그림 ③ 한글
